To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
germline TP5 3 mutations in French Canadian cancer families are rare.
TP53 mutations are not a major contributor of breast and/or ovarian cancers in French Canadian families.
germline TP5 3 mutations are not a major contributor in BRCA 1 and BRCA 2 mutation-negative breast cancer families of French-Canadian descent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the TP53 germline mutations and their role in the pathogenesis of breast cancer in French Canadian population.
the identification of genetic markers for breast cancer in the French Canadian population and the development of a genetic counseling program for women with breast cancer in this population.
the identification of genes involved in breast cancer predisposition in the French Canadian population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TP53 mutations are not major contributors to BRCA1/2 mutation-negative breast cancer families in French Canadians.
TP53 is a very minor contributor to breast and/or ovarian cancers in French Canadian families.
TP53 mutations are not a major contributor in French Canadian families with a high risk for hereditary breast and/or ovarian cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that TP53 mutations are not a major contributor in French Canadian breast cancer.
TP53 is a rare contributor to breast cancer in this population.
we identified TP53 as a rare contributor to breast cancer families of French-Canadian descent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TP53 14538 G-A mutation is a rare mutation in the population and is not associated with breast cancer risk.
TP53 mutations are not a major contributor in French Canadian breast cancer susceptibility.
the 13398G>A mutation in TP53 is a common cause of Li-Fraumenie-like (LFL).
